title: renewal-sprint-heatmap-facilitator-lab
content:
Purpose:
This working-lab doc defines a compact 30-minute renewal sprint format for mid-market and enterprise accounts focusing on a visual heatmap to accelerate renewal decisions. Intended for CSMs who need a lightweight, repeatable facilitation script and checklist to run a quick risk triage, align on remediation, and lock next-step owners.

When to use this sprint:
- Customer renewal is within 60 days and signal is ambiguous (usage has dipped or exec engagement is low).
- Account shows 1+ technical/regression flags but commercial signals are mixed.
- Quick alignment is required across CS, Solutions, and AE to avoid escalation.

Outcome (measurable):
- Shared heatmap snapshot captured in product notes and a follow-up ticket with owner and ETA within 24 hours.
- Decision among three outcomes: invest (action plan + SLO), monitor (30-day check-in), or escalate (AE exec alignment).

Preread for participants (send 48–72 hours prior):
- One-pager: top 3 usage metrics (30/90 day), recent latency/error incidents, open high-severity tickets (IDs).
- Last customer touch notes (CS activity log) and renewal date + ARR impact.
- Link to product dashboard + Live usage table.

Required roles and invites (compact):
- Facilitator (CSM) — runs the sprint and owns minutes.
- AE (optional for commercial clarifications).
- Product/SE or Solutions SME (for technical triage).
- SRE/Support on-call (if incidents are active).
- Executive sponsor (only if heatmap moves to red escalation).

Agenda (30 minutes) — fast cadence
1) 0:00–03:00 — Kick + framing (Facilitator)
- Quick hello, objective, and confirm decision process.
- Readout of pre-read highlights (CSM): renewal date, ARR, one-line health.

Script snippet: "We have 30 minutes to decide whether we need to invest additional resources, monitor, or escalate to AE exec touch. We'll use a heatmap to surface signals quickly; aim to leave with a single owner and next step."

2) 03:00–12:00 — Heatmap walkthrough (Facilitator + SME)
- Walk each heatmap lane (2 minutes per lane max). Call out thresholds and current value.
- Lanes: Adoption, Reliability, Feature Fit, Exec Engagement, ROI Signals.

Heatmap lane definitions and thresholds (facilitator shorthand):
- Adoption: 0–30% product-active-users = Red; 31–60% = Yellow; >60% = Green. Metric: active users / seat count or API calls per day.
- Reliability: >2 Sev1 incidents in 30d = Red; 1 Sev1 or 3 Sev2s = Yellow; otherwise Green.
- Feature Fit: Missing a required platform feature or major blocker in roadmap = Red; partial fit requiring workaround = Yellow; fit = Green.
- Exec Engagement: No executive contact in 90d = Red; sporadic check-ins = Yellow; active sponsorship = Green.
- ROI Signals: No clear business metric improvement (revenue, cost saved, retention) = Red; weak signals/indicative wins = Yellow; strong documented ROI = Green.

Heatmap guidance: mark each lane Red/Yellow/Green and annotate the most-likely cause (short phrase). Example: Adoption=Yellow (API key rotation caused drop).

3) 12:00–19:00 — Rapid triage and root-cause pairing
- For each Red/Yellow lane, ask: Why now? Who owns a fix? How long to remediate?
- Use a simple two-axis decision: Impact (High/Low) x Effort (High/Low).

Facilitator prompts (triage):
- "Which of these issues directly affects renewal economics in the next 60 days?"
- "If we did nothing, what is the likely customer reaction?"
- "Which fix is a single owner away versus requires cross-org coordination?"

4) 19:00–25:00 — Decide and assign
- Choose one of: Invest (green-light a focused play), Monitor (check in in 30 days), Escalate (AE exec alignment).
- Capture an action ticket with: action, owner, due date, required resources, and success criteria.

Decision rules (fast heuristics):
- If 2+ Red lanes and Impact=High -> Escalate to AE + Exec alignment.
- If 1 Red lane with Effort=Low and Impact=High -> Invest and open a targeted remediation ticket with 14d SLA.
- If all lanes Yellow or single Red but Impact=Low -> Monitor with 30-day check-in.

5) 25:00–30:00 — Commitments, closing script, and next steps
- Read back owner + ETA, confirm reporting cadence, and confirm follow-up meeting (if needed).
- Close with crisp next-step email commitment timebox: 24 hours for ticket creation; 48 hours for AE touch if escalated.

Facilitation script: language and escalation cues
- Opening: "Objective is a single, defensible decision. We’ll treat this as an evidence-driven sprint — we’ll lean on metrics and tickets, not opinions."
- If conversation stalls: "Let's park that deeper topic in a 30-minute follow-up and keep the decision in-sprint — we can surface the deeper work afterward."
- If SME says unknown: "Who can own a 48-hour spike to validate? If none, we default to Monitor and schedule a spike as an action."

Documentation and artifacts (what facilitator must capture):
- Heatmap snapshot image or table inserted into CS notes.
- Action ticket (Jira/Linear) with link in meeting minutes.
- One-paragraph customer-facing summary for AE to send (if escalation).

Follow-up templates (copy/paste):
- Internal action ticket title: "[Customer] Renewal Sprint — Remediation: <short action>"
- One-line meeting minutes (to paste into ticket): "Heatmap: A=Y, R=G, F=Y, E=R, ROI=Y. Decision: Invest — owner <name>, due <YYYY-MM-DD>."

Customer-facing follow-up email (AE/CS):
Subject: "Quick follow-up: next steps for <Customer> renewal"
Body: "Thanks again for the time today. We agreed to focus on <short action> to ensure <expected outcome>. Owner <name> will deliver an update by <date>. We'll reconvene if the remediation changes timeline."

Jira/Linear snippet for backlog (example):
- Title: [ACCT-<id>] Renewal remediation — API key rotation mitigation
- Description: Short bullet summary, severity, steps, test criteria, contact person, customer impact, expected release window.

Pre-meeting prep checklist (to run 48–72h before):
- Generate adoption chart: 30/90 day active users, API calls per hour/day, top 10 endpoints. (Dashboard: /dashboards/renewal/adoption)
- Pull incident list last 90 days (IDs + status).
- Confirm renewal date and ARR exposure in CRM (Salesforce).
- Collect last 3 CS touches and notes.
- Invite attendees and attach pre-read + heatmap template.

Post-meeting immediate steps (within 24h):
- Facilitator creates action ticket(s) and links to meeting notes.
- Send internal summary to AE, Solutions, and SRE.
- If Escalate chosen: AE sends the customer-facing email within 48h.

Quick escalation playbook (if escalate decision):
- AE: schedule 30-minute exec alignment with customer. Prepare 1-slide summary (heatmap + ask).
- CS: Prepare technical appendix and remediation timeline options (best-case/worst-case).
- Product/Solutions: commit to a decision window (48–72h) on feasibility of requested change.

Examples and short scenarios (lab practice prompts):
1) Scenario A: Adoption dropped 45% after single schema change. Heatmap: Adoption=Red, Reliability=Green, Feature Fit=Green, Exec Engagement=Yellow -> Decision: Invest (SE implements migration script, 7d).
2) Scenario B: Two Sev1 incidents in 30d and no exec contact -> Heatmap: Reliability=Red, Exec Engagement=Red -> Decision: Escalate (AE exec meeting + SRE hotfix).

Meeting minutes template (one paragraph to paste into notes):
- Date, attendees, heatmap (A/R/F/E/ROI values), decision (Invest/Monitor/Escalate), owners and due dates, open risks, follow-ups.

Facilitator quick heuristics cheat-sheet (one-liners):
- Always tie a Red lane to a concrete customer impact (revenue, uptime, churn risk).
- Prefer small experiments with owners over long ambiguous action items.
- If unsure, default to Monitor + Spike (48h) rather than unconstrained escalation.

Appendix A: Pre-read email (sample)
Subject: "Pre-read: 30m renewal sprint for <Customer> — <date/time>"
Hi team —
Attached: 1-page pre-read with adoption, incidents, and renewal date. Goal: make a fast decision on renewal posture and next steps. Please review before the meeting; bring any outstanding technical questions.

Appendix B: Heatmap ASCII template (paste into CS notes)
- Adoption: [Green|Yellow|Red] — key stat: <% active users>
- Reliability: [Green|Yellow|Red] — recent incidents: <IDs>
- Feature Fit: [Green|Yellow|Red] — blocker: <short phrase>
- Exec Engagement: [Green|Yellow|Red] — last contact: <date>
- ROI Signals: [Green|Yellow|Red] — metric: <revenue / cost saved / retention>

Notes and next steps: (facilitator fill-in)
1) Decision: <Invest / Monitor / Escalate>
2) Owner(s): <name(s)>
3) Due: <YYYY-MM-DD>
4) Ticket(s): <link(s)>

Usage guidance: treat this template as a sprint — keep time, keep alignment, and bias for creating a single actionable ticket that reduces ambiguity. This file is intentionally lean: copy, reuse, and adapt to account size and internal workflows.
